Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
752 AM EDT Tue Sep 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Issued a short fuse Coastal Flood Advisory for Southeast Harford
County (Havre de Grace) until 11 AM.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry through mid week.

- 2) Shower and thunderstorm chances return Thursday.

- 3) Cooler and less humid conditions are expected on 
     Friday, before humidity builds back in next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry through mid week.

Conditions will remain tranquil as high pressure persists over 
the Mid-Atlantic through Wednesday before gradually moving 
offshore. Large scale subsidence and dry air lead to a 
precipitation-free forecast with temperatures rising to several 
degrees above normal as the high pulls offshore. This leads to 
high temperatures in the mid to upper 80s today, perhaps near 
90 Wednesday (slightly cooler in the mountains). Low 
temperatures (and dew points) will generally be in the 50s and 
60s during this time. Some river valley fog is likely each 
morning.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Shower and thunderstorm chances return Thursday.

The upper-level ridge will begin to flatten out Wednesday before 
breaking down and pushing south and east into Thursday. Several 
pieces of upper-level energy rotating around an upper low 
centered over the Hudson Bay will slowly push a cold front south
towards our region by Thursday. At the surface, high pressure 
pushing offshore will bring increasingly warm and humid 
conditions to the area, with highs in the 80s to near 90 with 
dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s, with the highest values 
being Thursday.

Model guidance over the past 24 hours has come into better agreement 
in regards to the progression of the front on Thursday, as well as 
the upper-level pattern in association with it. The front 
really looks like it will flatten out as it moves southward, and
really loses the upper-level support. The timing of peak 
heating and the highest shear just doesn't look to line up at 
this point. There may be some jet-induced showers and storms 
late Thursday as we move into the right entrance of the upper 
jet centered over New England, but not necessarily expecting 
those to be severe at that point, as the front should be largely
through the region. At this point, the severe weather threat 
looks very limited, but any storm that develops on the warm side
of the boundary could bring some gusty winds along with it, but
the lack of a substantial wind field will really make that more
difficult with southward extent.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Cooler and less humid conditions are expected 
on Friday, before humidity builds back in next weekend. 

High pressure will build to our north on Friday in the wake of 
Thursday's frontal passage. Cooler and drier air will advect into 
the region from the north in advance of the approaching high. Mostly 
sunny skies are expected, with high temperatures in the upper 70s 
and lower 80s. It will also feel considerably less humid, with 
dewpoints dropping into the upper 50s and lower 60s.

High pressure will move offshore and a strong area of low pressure 
will track across Hudson Bay on Saturday, causing winds to turn out 
of the south in response. Southerly winds will advect a more humid 
airmass back into the area, with dewpoints climbing into the upper 
60s and lower 70s. Chances for afternoon showers and thunderstorms 
will accompany the more humid airmass. Both instability and shear 
values are forecast to remain low, so any storms that do form are 
expected to stay on the weaker side.

Model guidance begins to diverge a bit by Sunday and Monday, but 
most solutions favor continued above average temperatures, with 
highs in the mid to upper 80s. Ensemble guidance suggests that 
chances for afternoon showers and thunderstorms should trend 
downward as Saturday's system tracks further east across Canada 
within zonal flow, but there are a few solutions (such as the 12z 
Canadian) that favor a more amplified longwave pattern and greater 
chances for showers and thunderstorms.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected to prevail through the end of the
week, with two exceptions. Early morning river valley fog could
affect mainly KCHO/KMRB each day roughly 08z-13z. Then, some
shower and thunderstorm activity could bring brief restrictions
on Thursday (mainly in the afternoon and/or evening). Light 
winds become S today, then remain S through Thursday until a 
cold front brings a shift to W/NW.

Prevailing VFR conditions are expected on Friday and Saturday, 
although a passing thunderstorm can't be ruled out Saturday 
afternoon. Winds will generally be light out of the north to 
northwest on Friday, and then light out of the south to southeast
on Saturday.

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will result in light northeast winds becoming
south through Tuesday. Winds may increase briefly early
Wednesday morning as the high shifts offshore, but are more
likely to increase in southerly channeling Wednesday afternoon
into Wednesday night. Winds shift to the west and northwest and
could remain gusty Thursday as a cold front crosses, possibly
bringing a few showers and thunderstorms. 

Sub-SCA level north to northwesterly winds are expected over 
the waters on Friday. Winds will shift to out of the south on 
Saturday, and could near low-end SCA levels within channeled 
southerly flow Saturday afternoon into Saturday evening.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tide levels remain around 1 to 1.25 feet above normal. With 
light northeast winds becoming southerly, tide levels are likely
to remain relatively steady around 1 foot above astronomical 
norms through the middle of the week. Annapolis could reach
Minor Stage one or two more times through Thursday prior to a 
cold front shifting winds to the west. Other sites could 
approach minor flood at times, as well, with Havre de Grace
expected to be right at the minor threshold this morning.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Coastal Flood Advisory until 11 AM EDT this morning for MDZ508.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.
